title: Ranking

script.script:
MATCHUP 1

Automated Voice: "Freezing kits vs Cutting with nail clippers."

Speaker: "Freezing kits. Cutting bleeds way more than you think and can get infected. Freezing at least doesn't leave you bandaging your neck for a week."

MATCHUP 2

Automated Voice: "Tying off with dental floss vs Skin tag patches."

Speaker: "Patches. Tying it off is basically DIY surgery. It swells, it hurts, and if it gets infected now you've got a real problem. Patches at least don't make it worse."


MATCHUP 3

Automated Voice: "Freezing kits vs Skin tag patches."

Speaker: "Freezing. Patches leave a sticky sore spot and the tag's usually still there. Freezing works but it hurts pretty bad."


MATCHUP 4

Automated Voice: "Dermatologist removal vs Freezing kits."

Speaker: "Dermatologist. Freezing at home is hit or miss. The dermatologist actually gets it done. But it's a couple hundred dollars per tag and a waiting list just to get in."


MATCHUP 5

Automated Voice: "Skin tag patches vs Dermatologist removal."

Speaker: "Oh this one's hard. Dermatologist. Patches rarely work. But the dermatologist leaves a tiny scar for every single one and that adds up fast."


MATCHUP 6

Automated Voice: "Dermatologist removal vs Castor oil."

Speaker: "Castor oil no question. Dermatologist works but it's expensive and you get a scar for every tag. Castor oil soaks down to the root and the ricinoleic acid cuts off the blood supply. It dries out shrinks and falls off on its own. No pain no bleeding no scars."


FINAL

Automated Voice: "Freezing kits vs Castor oil."

Speaker: "Easy. Freezing hurts and half the time the tag grows back. Castor oil works from the inside out. It actually gets to the root so the tag falls off and stays gone."


CTA

Speaker: "I use Haven and Spool because it's organic cold pressed and hexane free. Comes in dark amber glass with a rose quartz roller. You just roll it on the skin tag before bed and let it work while you sleep. They're doing buy one get one free right now and you can try it for 30 nights or it's free. Link's below."

open_notes.note:
Hey @Johnny, I made two versions so we can test both:

H1 follows the script exactly, as a bracket. While building it, the matchups didn't fit a bracket. In a real bracket every item shows up once and the loser is out, but here some come back. Patches lose in matchup 3 and play again in matchup 5. Freezing loses to the dermatologist in matchup 4 and is still in the final. Castor oil appears straight into round 6 without winning a round first. So the bracket shows the same items on both sides, and castor oil seems to come out of nowhere, which looks off.

H2 is the alternative: same script, same edit. Each matchup gets its own versus card: the two items side by side, the winner turns green and the loser red, and castor oil gets crowned in gold at the end. Nothing repeats, so it reads cleanly.

Pick whichever you prefer, or we can run both and let the numbers decide.
